hook_text: 4 matches, then 7, then 10. Why not 4, 8, 12? The answer is a shared side.
clip_script: Mbombela, a maths display. One square: 4 matches. Two squares side by side: 7. Three: 10. Each new square borrows a side, so it adds only 3. Rule: shape number times 3, plus 1. Shape 10: 31 matches. Shape 20? Not double 31. Use the rule: 61. Now dots in triangles: 1, 3, 6, 10. The jumps grow: 2, 3, 4. Next jump 5: 15 dots. And folded paper: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 layers. Same jump, growing jumps, doubling. Count, look at the jumps, find the rule.
visual_style: Matchstick squares building in a row with the shared side glowing, then dot triangles adding new rows.
mood: Curious, like solving a puzzle at a science fair.
pacing: Build three squares, reveal the shared side, jump to shape 20, then the faster patterns.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and invent a matchstick pattern with its own rule.
